Mandatory military training
to youths

SHARDA:
SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
impart mandatory military training to the
youths of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) by when a final decision in this regard
is likely to be taken;

Killings in J&K
*41. SHRI SWARAJ KAUSHAL: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) what are the comparative figures of
terrorist acts by J&K militants each year
during the last three years;
(b) the number of security personnel
killed and wounded by J&K militants each
year during the last three years;
(c) the number of civilian lives lost each
year during the last three years; and
(d) the number of J&K terrorists killed
each year during the last three years?
Busting of international drug
racket
*42. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in the context of recent
busting of an international drug racket in
Kolkata, the Interpol experts have
commented that enforcement of legally
grown poppy has been traditionally effective
in India;

Funds to Himachal Pradesh under
IWDP, DPAP, DDP and TDET
†*44. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the amount provided to Himachal
Pradesh during the last two years under the
Integrated Wasteland Development
Programme (IWDP), Drought Prone Area
Programme (DPAP), Desert Development
Programme (DDP) and Technology
Development Extension and Training
(TDET) implemented under the control of
Land Resources Department of Rural
Development Ministry; and
(b) the manner in which the State
Government have utilised this amount?
Deteriorating power situation in Delhi
*45. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
DR. AKHILESH DAS:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether despite plentiful power
supply to the Capital, it suffered from
frequent and prolonged power break- downs
during the last summer months;
(b) if so, whether this was attributable to
the fragile transmission and distribution
system;
(c) the reasons for not updating and
augmenting the T&D system;
(d) whether it is a fact that with the
privatisation of distribution and sale of
power, the power supply position has
deteriorated and billing system has
collapsed; and
(e) if so, the reasons for privatisation?
Low cost housing for textile workers
*46. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have taken up
building of low cost houses for textile
workers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Violations of traffic rules in
Delhi
*47. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the drivers in
Delhi flout the no-entry rule and drive at
high speed at night resulting in frequent
accidents and tragedies;
(b) whether the present strength of traffic
police is sufficient to meet the traffic
requirement in the city; and
(c) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to man the roads in the wee
hours?

district of Andhra Pradesh on 16.6.03;

Review of coal royalty
†280. SHRI SUREDSH PACHOURI:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is a provision of
reviewing the royalty rate of coal in very
three year;
(b) whether after 1994 the coal royalty
in M.P. has been reviewed in the year 2002;
(c) whether as per the instructions of
11th Finance Commission in case of the
absence of the review of royalty-rates by
the Government of India the losses suffered
by the states will be compensated by the
central Government;
(d) if so, losses suffered by M.P. in the
absence of the review of the royalty rate for
such a long time; and
(e) by when the compensation amount
would be paid by Government to M.P. as
per the recommendations made by the 11th
Finance Commission?
Investigation into C.I.L. affairs
281. SHRI SANJAY NIRUMPAM:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether CBI has recently
investigated the affairs of coal India Ltd.
(CIL); and
(b) if so, the details of the investigation
and action taken in this regard?
Safety of coalmine workers
282. SHRI G.K. VASAN: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken to ensure safety of
coalmine workers; and
(b) whether any proposal to increase the
compensation is under consideration?
Development of Coalmines for capture
purpose
283. SHRI C.P.
THIRUNAVUKKARRASU: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government ave reviewed
the impact of the order authorising
Government companies or undertakings to
do regular coal or lignite mining;
(b) if so, the response given by the
States;
(c) whether Government are considering
to allow developing coal maines for captive
purpose:

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Reduction in coal quota to Sarni
Thermal Power Plant
†284. SHRI SRESH PACHOURI: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the quota of
coal of Sarni Thermal Power Plant has been
reduced to 5.5 lakh metric tonnes per month
from the present 6 lakh metric tonnes per
month during April, 2003;
(b) whether PUF of Sarni Thermal
Power Plant has fallen from 80 per cent to
70 per cent and power generation has been
reduced by 250 mega watt as a result of
supply of less supply of coal to the said
plant;
(c) whether the Government of Madhya
Pradesh have requested to increase coal
linkage of Sarni Thermal Power Plant to
6.5 lakhs metric tonnes per month; and
(d) whether Government propose to
extend assistance to Madhya Pradesh to raise
power generation by accepting this
proposal?
Coal supplied by WCL to Madhya
Pradesh Vidyut Mandal
†285. SHRI SURESH PACHOURI:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Madhya
Pradesh Vidyut Mandal has brought to the
notice of Western Coalfield that coal supplied
by them is not of good quality:
(b) whether stone contents in this coal
are very high:
(c) if so, the action being taken to make
improvement in the same; and
(d) whether the coal company propose
to compensate for the losses incurred to
Madhya Pradesh Vidyut Mandal for not
suppling good quality of coal?
Requirement of coal by power plants
†286. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of coal being used for
generation of power in the country;
(b) the revenue earned therefrom;
(c) the quantum of coal required by
various power plants based on coal during
the Ninth Plan Period and the quantum of
coal supplied to the said plants;
(d) whether Government have made any
assessment with regard to demand of coal
by these power plants during the Tenth Plan
period; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Increase in coal production during
Tenth Plan
†287. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken to enhance the
production of coal to meet the requirement
of power plants and industrial units during
Tenth Plan; and
(b) the steps being taken by Government
of enhance production capacity of coal mine
workers?
